paper.title_en: Resonant Cavity Searches for Millicharged Dark Matter
paper.abstract_en: A plethora of resonant cavity experiments have been designed to search for ultralight dark matter (DM) candidates, such as axion or dark-photon DM. In this work, we show that these same apparatuses can be sensitive to ultralight millicharged dark matter (mDM) with masses $m_φ\sim1-100\,μ\mathrm{eV}$. Similar to axion DM, in the presence of a background magnetic field, mDM acts as an effective current which can excite the modes of a resonant cavity. Importantly, for a cylindrical cavity, axion DM dominantly couples to the transverse magnetic (TM) modes, whereas mDM dominantly couples to the transverse electric (TE) modes. We project the sensitivity to mDM that resonant cavity experiments can achieve if they are able to tune and readout their TE modes. We find that fractional millicharges as small as $ε_m=e_m/e\sim10^{-19}$ can be probed. If mDM constitutes only a subfraction $f_\mDM \lesssim0.2\%$ of the total DM density, competing astrophysical bounds do not apply. In this case, resonant cavities can be the most sensitive probes of mDM in this mass range.
